rationale: The redesign replaces a speculative two-sided booking marketplace with a demand-anchored managed-capacity operator. The hypothesis is that a route-specific anchor fleet will accept a take-or-pay minimum before any host capacity is activated; that commitment then gates exclusive site-window and physical-bay rights, monitored uptime, service credits, and contracted fallback capacity delivered through an incumbent compliant charging stack. This changes utilization risk, capital sequencing, pricing, distribution, and the control point while preserving the evidence that local demand, host rights, charger compatibility, operating costs, and willingness to pay remain unvalidated.
